_comment: DECLARED GAPS of the design bindings ledger: a binding whose proof depends on a shadow-oracle
cell that CANNOT BE RECORDED on the machine the golden was made on. The owner has looked at each
one and decided the cell is right, the binding is right, and the missing thing is a backend.
Same shape of decision as testing/llm-conformance/named-gaps.json, and the same rules:
* A DECLARED GAP IS NEVER A PASS. The binding is reported GAP -- its own verdict, its own
column, its own line in the gate's output -- and never folded into the pass count. `--check`
and `--check --strict` both keep it out of the owed set, exactly as a named gap is kept out
everywhere else in this tree, so a gap is reported rather than masked and rather than red.
* A GAP FORGIVES ONLY WHAT IT NAMES. `cells` is the exact list of cell ids this entry excuses
on this binding. Any OTHER check of that binding that settles nothing leaves the binding FAIL,
unchanged. An entry cannot widen itself by being vague: a cell not named here is not forgiven.
* AN UNUSED ENTRY IS A LIE. An entry whose named cells are not actually failing on that binding
today -- the backend arrived, the cell was recorded, the citation was dropped -- is RED, and
the fix is to DELETE the entry, never to leave it standing as a waiver nothing needs.
* THE CEILING IS ASSERTED, NOT OBSERVED. `expected` is the number of gaps the owner has agreed
to carry. Exceeding it is RED with no further argument: a register that silently grows is a
way of turning a gate off one row at a time.
Checked by scripts/design-bindings.py (--verify-gaps, and the GAP verdict it hands the shell
gate); the arms above each have a case in scripts/design-bindings.sh --selftest.

gaps.id: DBG-1 store-mysql and store-valkey on the ABI-2 audit/denylist fallback
gaps.reason: The binding is proven on the two backends this host can reach: plugins.store-persist|store-sqlite (no fixture needed) and plugins.store-persist|store-postgres (recorded against a live postgres once the fixture env var existed), plus the two adapter unit tests that pin the rule itself -- only TransportErrorKind::Unsupported opens a default, on the four audit/denylist verbs, and every other failure shape propagates. What is missing is a SERVER: the mysql cell is gated on BUSBAR_TEST_MYSQL_URL and the valkey cell on VALKEY_URL, and neither backend runs on the machine the pinned 1.5.5 golden was recorded on, so both cells stand SKIP on golden/1.5.5/ledger.tsv with the reason 'named gap: the fixture this cell needs is not in the tree yet'. Recording them would need the same published 1.5.5 binary run against a live mysql and a live valkey. Delete this entry the day either fixture lands: the cell is already defined, already bound to this row, and turns from a gap into a recording the moment its env var is set -- which is exactly what happened to store-postgres.

gaps.id: DBG-2 store-mysql and store-valkey on the 1.6.0-only store-op shim
gaps.reason: Same two unrecordable backends, same reason, on the binding that says a 1.5.5-era store boots and serves byte-identically because every 1.6.0-only operation is answered by a node-local shim. The claim is proven on store-sqlite and store-postgres, which are recorded, and by the two adapter unit tests that pin the shim's two halves -- Unsupported alone opens the inert default, and a real answer passes through untouched. The mysql and valkey cells would widen the same proof to two more backends; they are gated on BUSBAR_TEST_MYSQL_URL and VALKEY_URL and stand SKIP on the pinned golden for want of a server, not for want of a check. Delete this entry when either fixture lands.
